intro: Welcome to Iasos, an ancient city in Muğla province, with roots in the 2nd millennium BC. This harbour town on a peninsula was famed for its fishing, and for the blue-and-white veined marble that Rome sold as cipollino.
history: This harbour town on a peninsula lived by fishing and by the blue-and-white veined marble it quarried, which was sold in Rome as cipollino and used in imperial buildings. Its story is older still: traces of settlement go back to the second millennium BC and the Mycenaean period.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the agora and the theatre. Then find the fish market, and walk out to the Roman mole.
facts: Did you know? Ancient writers tell of Iasian fishermen so single-minded that a famous musician's recital emptied the moment the fish-market bell rang. And the city's blue-and-white veined marble was sold in Rome as cipollino and used in imperial buildings.
outro: This brings our tour of Iasos to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Enjoy your visit.
